channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Partidos apresentam nova ação ao STF para derrubar dosimetria que beneficia Bolsonaro
item.description: The Brazil of Hope Federation, comprising PT, PCdoB and PV, filed an action at the STF to overturn the Dosimetry Law, which reduced Bolsonaro’s penalties in electoral cases. The coalition claims the law is unconstitutional and unfairly benefits the former president. The initiative aims to restore the original sanctions imposed for abuse of political power and misuse of media.

item.title: O contrato de R$ 90 milhões para publicidade do Senado
item.description: The Senate signed a R$ 90 million contract with two advertising agencies — Cálix Propaganda and CC&P — to promote its activities over an initial one-year term, renewable up to nine times. Cálix is managed by Marcello Lopes, who is reportedly being considered for a role in Senator Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign. The stated goal is to increase public awareness of the Senate’s functions, areas of work, and enacted laws.

item.title: Oposição articula PEC da Anistia após Moraes suspender Lei da Dosimetria
item.description: The opposition in Congress is pushing for the 'Amnesty PEC' after Justice Alexandre de Moraes of the STF suspended the Dosimetry Law, which had reduced sentences for those convicted in the January 8, 2023 attacks. PL leader Sóstenes Cavalcante says he has filed the proposal and is gathering signatures to meet the constitutional threshold (171 deputies and 27 senators) to initiate formal debate. The move is framed as a response to the judicial blockage of the congressional-approved sentence reduction.

item.title: Bolsonarista e petista brigam em palco de festa agro após elogio a Bolsonaro
item.description: During the Festa das Nações in Mato Grosso do Sul, federal deputy Rodolfo Nogueira (PL) praised former president Jair Bolsonaro and was confronted by PT councilwoman Eliete Feitosa, who knocked off his hat on stage. The incident followed Nogueira’s claim that Bolsonaro was unjustly imprisoned and barred from running for office, sparking a heated exchange in which other men on stage restrained Feitosa as she protested. Nogueira concluded by shouting 'out with Lula' and shared the video on social media, claiming he was assaulted, while Feitosa has not issued a public statement.

item.title: Governo cancela reunião sobre aumento da mistura nos combustíveis
item.description: The Ministry of Mines and Energy canceled the CNPE meeting that was to discuss raising the mandatory ethanol blend in gasoline from 30% (E30) to 32% (E32) and biodiesel in diesel from 15% (B15) to 16% (B16), postponing the deliberation without setting a new date. This comes despite recent statements by President Lula indicating the government was poised to announce the change, with E32 technical viability tests already advanced and B16 studies expected to begin in May. The increase is mandated by the 2024 Future Fuel Law, but has faced delays, while the biofuels sector views rising fossil fuel prices as an ideal moment to boost domestic production and reduce import dependence.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro, Caiado e Zema criticam decisão de Moraes sobre o PL da Dosimetria
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) and Romeu Zema (Novo) criticized the decision by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes to suspend the Dosimetry Law, calling it an invasion of power, judicial activism, and a threat to democracy. They argued that the suspension diverts attention from real public issues such as security, education, and health. Moraes’ decision was based on two actions challenging the law’s constitutionality, which are to be judged by the Supreme Court’s Plenary.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro reage a Salles após ex-ministro acusá-lo de ter vendido vaga em chapa ao Senado a aliado do PL
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro (PL) rebutted accusations from Ricardo Salles (Novo-SP), who alleged he sold his support for André do Prado (PL) in São Paulo’s Senate slate. Eduardo said Salles is acting out of spite for not being selected as the PL’s candidate and called him a 'political windbiruta,' stating he won’t sue but demanded proof of any financial deal. Eduardo is the first substitute on Prado’s Senate ticket.

item.title: Oposição amplia pressão sobre STF após decisão de Alexandre de Moraes
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes of the STF temporarily suspended the Dosimetry Law, which reduced sentences for those convicted in the January 8 attacks, triggering a new escalation in political tensions between the opposition and the judiciary. The move has intensified polarization and is being used by opposition figures as electoral fuel, with candidates like Romeu Zema, Ronaldo Caiado, and Flávio Bolsonaro calling for stronger stances against the Court. Bolsonarist leaders are pushing for amnesty via constitutional amendment (PEC) to mobilize their base.

item.title: Dosimetria: foi o STF ou os militares de alta patente que evitaram o golpe?
item.description: The text questions whether reducing penalties for those involved in the January 8 attacks truly threatens democracy, arguing that on that date, there was no concrete risk of a coup, as the golpist movement had already been defeated and Bolsonaro was isolated. It suggests Bolsonaro’s arrest may have been driven by the fake news inquiry led by Alexandre de Moraes, whose actions — despite alleged excesses — are seen by some as necessary to preserve the Rule of Law. However, military testimonies indicate that the refusal of high-ranking armed forces officials to support a coup in December 2022 was decisive in preventing institutional rupture, challenging the narrative of the STF as the sole savior of democracy.

item.title: Zema satiriza Ciro Nogueira, Vorcaro e Janja em “Os Intocáveis”
item.description: Romeu Zema, pre-candidate for president from the Novo party, released the sixth episode of his satirical series 'Os Intocáveis', targeting Senator Ciro Nogueira, Banco Master founder Daniel Vorcaro, and First Lady Rosângela da Silva (Janja) using AI-generated puppets. The video references PF investigations into alleged monthly payments of R$300,000 to R$500,000 to Nogueira, Vorcaro’s plea deal, Janja’s R$117 million in public spending, and STF ministers like Dias Toffoli. The series, inactive since April 25, returns with allusions to the Banco Master case and the fake news inquiry involving Gilmar Mendes and Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: Clima tenso: Ricardo Salles dispara contra Eduardo Bolsonaro e Valdemar da Costa Neto
item.description: Former Minister Ricardo Salles (Novo-SP), a pre-candidate for the Senate in São Paulo, accused Eduardo Bolsonaro (PL-SP) of harming Brazil through his actions in the U.S., including alleged involvement in the 'tariff war,' and claimed Eduardo stayed abroad by choice with family financial support. Salles also criticized Valdemar da Costa Neto, PL president, for the party’s Senate slate, questioning the nomination of André do Prado and Eduardo as a potential substitute. Eduardo Bolsonaro responded in a YouTube video, saying he expected Salles’ attack and that the lack of Bolsonaro family support undermines the former ally’s electoral chances.

item.title: Dino defende decisões individuais no STF e participação de ministros em eventos
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino defended the legitimacy of individual decisions within the court and the participation of judges in public hearings and events. He emphasized that such actions are essential for the democratic functioning of the Judiciary and do not constitute an overreach of power.

item.title: Governo Lula investirá R$ 11 bi em plano contra o crime organizado
item.description: President Lula’s government announced the Brazil Against Organized Crime Program, with R$ 11 billion in investment (R$ 1 billion from the Federal Budget and R$ 10 billion via BNDES for states), set to launch on May 12, 2026. The initiative includes six action axes, such as intelligence integration and prison system control, and requires state adherence to access funds. Announced by Minister José Guimarães, it underscores the administration’s focus on combating organized crime as a key Planalto priority.

item.title: Fachin fala em ‘esgotamento histórico’ e ‘ressignificar’ o papel dos juízes
item.description: The president of the Supreme Federal Court (STF), Minister Edson Fachin, stated that it is time to redefine the role of the judiciary amid a context of permanent tension, crises, and a sense of historical exhaustion, advocating for defending institutions without idolatry and building public trust beyond cynicism or naivety. He referenced Carlos Drummond de Andrade’s 1945 interview to draw parallels with historical value shifts, such as the Estado Novo and European totalitarianism, and highlighted internal challenges like resistance to rulings on supersalaries and external criticism of ministers’ conduct in scandals and via injunctions.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro escolhe amigo empresário para comandar comunicação da campanha; veja quem é
item.description: Marcello Lopes, a close friend and businessman of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), has been appointed to coordinate the communications strategy for Flávio’s 2026 presidential campaign. Lopes, who was already part of the pre-campaign team, plans to bring in a team of media and advertising professionals, including former executives from Bates Worldwide, Grupo Abril, and Veja magazine, and is in advanced talks with Record’s journalism director, Roberto Munhoz. His team has already crafted slogans used by Flávio, such as comparing Lula to an 'old Opala' and 'expired product,' which drew a public rebuttal from the president.

item.title: Crusoé: Chegou a Turma do Milhão Mágico
item.description: The Canta Direita YouTube channel released two satirical videos targeting Brazilian politicians and STF justices, continuing the humorous tone started with 'Funk do Pilili,' which mocked the TSE mascot. The content is part of a parody series critiquing public figures and institutions.

item.title: Nikolas propõe ampliar poder da Câmara para fiscalizar o STF
item.description: Deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) has proposed a bill to expand the Chamber of Deputies' oversight power over the Judiciary, Public Ministry, and audit courts, allowing lawmakers to demand administrative information with response deadlines and potential penalties for refusal or false data. The initiative aims to enhance transparency and republican control over institutions currently seen as autonomous, without interfering in judicial rulings. The proposal comes amid the deputy's criticism of STF decisions, such as Minister Alexandre de Moraes' suspension of the Dosimetry Law.

item.title: Nogueira e Janja se unem ao STF no 6º episódio de ‘Os Intocáveis’
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) released the sixth episode of the animated series Os Intocáveis, which satirizes Supreme Court justices. The episode features Nogueira and Janja united with the STF. This is the second release since STF dean Gilmar Mendes requested Zema’s inclusion in the fake news inquiry.

item.title: Fachin diz que Judiciário pode ser alvo de críticas e deve ser resiliente diante de ataques 'infundados'
item.description: Supreme Court President Edson Fachin defended the Judiciary as a legitimate target of constructive criticism but stressed the need for resilience against unfounded attacks, amid controversies involving ministers like Dias Toffoli and Alexandre de Moraes linked to banker Daniel Vorcaro. He urged the judiciary to maintain serenity, firmness, and wisdom to preserve its institutional essence. The remarks were made at the opening of a preparatory meeting for the 20th National Meeting of the Judiciary.

item.title: Lula veta lei que reconhece estágio como experiência profissional
item.description: President Lula vetoed a bill that would have recognized internships as professional experience for public sector exams, arguing it overlooks the pedagogical nature of internships and undermines selection criteria. The veto was based on constitutional concerns, as the bill generically assigned regulatory authority to the Public Power, centralizing competence exclusively in the presidency and violating federal autonomy and the independence of powers. The bill, approved by Congress in April, aimed to ease young people's access to their first job by counting internship experience.

item.title: STF deve manter validade da Lei da Dosimetria mesmo após suspensão determinada por Moraes
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) tends to uphold the validity of the Dosimetry Law, despite the suspension ordered by Alexandre de Moraes, which was seen as a 'housekeeping brake' to ensure legal security. Ministers indicate that adjustments may be made, but total invalidation is unlikely, as Congress holds the prerogative to define penalties, despite concerns about procedural flaws. There is no sign of a new confrontation with Congress at this time.

item.title: Medo de violência política atinge 6 a cada 10 brasileiros, aponta estudo
item.description: A study by the Brazilian Forum of Public Security shows that 59.6% of Brazilians aged 16 or older fear physical aggression due to their political choices, affecting approximately 99.4 million people. Although this figure has decreased from 68% in 2022, 2.2% of the population reported being victims of political violence in the past year, with higher impact among women, lower-income classes (D and E), and areas with criminal factions or militias.

item.title: Taxa das blusinhas: arrecadação sobe 25% e bate recorde; governo discute acabar com imposto
item.description: The government collected R$1.78 billion in import taxes during the first four months of 2026, a 25% increase from the same period in 2025, driven by the 'blusinhas tax' of 20% on international purchases under US$50. Finance Minister Dario Durigan confirmed the tax’s abolition is under internal discussion, despite industry support and the Remessa Conforme program. Introduced in 2024 to level the playing field between domestic and imported goods, the tax faces opposition and consumer criticism for raising prices on low-value items.

item.title: Moraes acerta ao suspender Lei da Dosimetria, mas STF tem de julgar rápido ações sobre constitucionalidade
item.description: Justice Alexandre de Moraes suspended the Dosimetry Law, which reduced sentences for those convicted in the January 8 attacks, pending the STF's ruling on its constitutionality. Two actions, filed by ABI and the Rede-Psol federation, challenge provisions such as non-cumulative penalties for democracy-related offenses and changes to penal regime progression. The opposition criticizes the law and threatens a constitutional amendment for broad amnesty, while government supporters praise it as a penal relief.

item.title: Como suspensão da Ypê pela Anvisa virou tema de disputa política nas redes
item.description: Anvisa suspended batches of Ypê products due to microbiological contamination risk, but the measure was temporarily reversed after the company's appeal. The incident quickly became a political flashpoint, with Bolsonaro supporters accusing the Lula government of persecution due to the Ypê-owning family's donations to Bolsonaro's 2022 campaign. On social media, influencers and politicians, including São Paulo's vice mayor, posted videos supporting the brand, turning a health issue into an ideological battle.

item.title: Pedro Cardoso mantém voto em Lula mesmo com “esperança frustrada”
item.description: Pedro Cardoso said he will vote for Lula in the 2026 elections, despite his initial hopes being partially frustrated. He acknowledges progress in democracy and historical injustices but criticizes the persistence of economic inequality, inherited through class and privilege, and ideological manipulation that leads the oppressed to support their own oppressor.

item.title: Zema critica “saidinha de Dia das Mães” no Rio de Janeiro
item.description: Romeu Zema, pre-candidate of Novo for the Presidency, criticized on X the 'Mother's Day furlough' in Rio de Janeiro, arguing that while working mothers live in fear, the system releases criminals. He advocated for a security department in the Ministry of Justice led by police officers and the use of body cameras in special operations, but not in daily patrols.

item.title: Flávio diz que vai “cuidar das mulheres” durante ato em SC
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) criticized the Lula government for rising feminicide rates in Brazil, claiming the administration 'talks the talk but doesn't walk the walk' on women's protection. Speaking at a PL event in Santa Catarina, he linked his and his father Jair Bolsonaro's administrations to pro-women policies, citing doubled Auxílio Brasil for single mothers and a record in arrests of aggressors. Flávio pledged to 'care for women', especially single mothers, in a speech delivered on Saturday (May 9) and shared on X (formerly Twitter) on Sunday (May 10).

item.title: Luiza Trajano explica Hino Nacional nas suas lojas e fala de ‘convite’ de Lula
item.description: Luiza Helena Trajano explained in her Gramado Summit speech that she implemented the national anthem every Monday across all 1,500 Magazine Luiza stores to foster patriotism and national self-esteem, noting initial skepticism from younger employees but now universal participation. She firmly denied rumors of being invited by Lula to serve as his vice president or join his government, stating she is not a candidate for any political office and belongs to no party, while identifying herself as a political actor through her advocacy for public policies via the Grupo Mulheres do Brasil, focusing on ending violence and inequality.

item.title: Neymar na Copa? Jogador inicia semana decisiva e tem duplo desafio contra Coritiba antes da convocação; veja cenário
item.description: Neymar faces a decisive week with matches against Coritiba in the Copa do Brasil and Brasileirão, aiming to prove his fitness for a potential call-up in Carlo Ancelotti's preliminary list for the 2026 World Cup. The Santos forward was praised by Spanish outlet AS for his goal and performance against Red Bull Bragantino, highlighting that he 'refuses to give up' in his bid for a spot on the Brazil national team.

item.title: O poder individual no Supremo Tribunal Federal
item.description: The article contends that monocratic decisions in the Brazilian Supreme Court (STF) stem from constitutional and legal design, not authoritarian tendencies or personalism of justices. Despite the high volume of individual rulings, the STF maintains robust collegial activity, averaging 2,368 cases per month in plenary and chambers — exceeding the annual caseload of many courts worldwide. Therefore, the balance between individual and collective acts reflects the functional structure of the judiciary, not an abuse of power.

item.title: Zema mantém embate e publica mais um capítulo da série que irritou Gilmar
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and pre-candidate for president under the Novo party, announced he will release a new episode of a video series on Monday (11) that has irritated Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes. The series has drawn criticism from Mendes, who views it as inappropriate and potentially harmful to democratic debate. Zema insists on maintaining the confrontation, defending freedom of expression and the need to question established institutions.

item.title: Governo Tarcísio aplica multa de R$ 1 bi à Fast Shop por fraude no ICMS e propina a auditor fiscal
item.description: The government of Tarcísio de Freitas fined Fast Shop R$1.04 billion for tax fraud and paying R$422 million in bribes to a São Paulo State Treasury auditor, involving undue ICMS refunds between 2021 and 2025. The fine, the largest ever applied in Brazil under the Anti-Corruption Law, followed Operation Ícaro and requires immediate payment and publication in a major newspaper.

item.title: Thiago Ávila chega em SP nesta 2ª feira após prisão em Israel
item.description: Brazilian Palestinian rights activist Thiago Ávila arrived in São Paulo on Monday (May 11, 2026) after being deported from Israel, where he had been detained since April 29 for participating in the Global Sumud Flotilla humanitarian mission to Gaza. He was intercepted in international waters, subjected to prolonged interrogations by Israeli intelligence services using alleged coercive methods and threats, and only released following pressure from President Lula, who called his detention 'unjustifiable'.

item.title: 41,2% dos brasileiros dizem conviver com o crime organizado
item.description: The "Fear of Crime and Elections 2026" report reveals that 41.2% of Brazilians aged 16 or older recognize the presence of organized criminal groups in their neighborhoods, equivalent to 68.7 million people. Conducted by Datafolha for the Brazilian Forum of Public Security, the study shows that organized crime has expanded beyond major capitals through territorial diffusion, affecting the routines of 57% of the population and increasing victimization rates to 51.1% in areas dominated by criminal factions.

item.title: Investigadores revisitam traumas da Lava-Jato para tentar não repetir erros no caso Master
item.description: The lawyer for Daniel Vorcaro, José Luís Oliveira Lima (Juca), met with TSE Minister Floriano de Azevedo Marques, an ally of Alexandre de Moraes, at a Brasília hotel last Wednesday (6) to discuss legal strategies aimed at avoiding the investigative mistakes of Operation Lava-Jato in the Master case.

item.title: Governo deve lançar programa contra o crime organizado nesta semana
item.description: The federal government is set to launch the 'Brazil Against Organized Crime' program next Tuesday (12), with R$ 11 billion in funding (R$ 1 billion from the budget and R$ 10 billion via BNDES loan). The initiative includes axes such as arms trafficking combat, financial suffocation of organized crime, increased homicide clearance rates, and prison security upgrades, including cell phone blockers and modern X-ray equipment. Implementation depends on state adherence, which would grant access to federal funds.

item.title: Nunes Marques e Mendonça assumem TSE, abrindo nova fase da Corte
item.description: Kassio Nunes Marques assumes the presidency of the TSE in an anticipated succession from Cármen Lúcia, with a mandate until May 2028, to be followed by André Mendonça until 2030. Both were appointed by Jair Bolsonaro and are expected to oversee the 2026 and 2028 elections with a profile of discretion and impartiality. Cármen Lúcia’s departure opens the seat for Dias Toffoli to return to the TSE, marking a shift in the Court’s composition, which will not have another woman in the presidency until at least 2042.

item.title: Lula deve anunciar quase R$ 1 bilhão em investimentos na Segurança Pública nesta semana
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is set to announce this week a nearly R$1 billion investment package for public security actions, focusing on combating organized crime, arms trafficking, and improving the prison system. The funds will be allocated to the National Public Security Fund and the National Penitentiary Fund via a decree and four ordinances. The announcement comes amid growing pressure for concrete results in security, especially ahead of the 2026 elections and in the context of international cooperation against organized financial crime.

item.title: Presidenciáveis da direita sobem tom contra Moraes por barrar Lei da Dosimetria, e oposição mira retomar debate da anistia
item.description: Right-wing presidential contenders, including Flávio Bolsonaro, Romeu Zema, and Ronaldo Caiado, intensified criticism of Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes after the STF suspended the Dosimetry Law, which reduced sentences for January 8 convicts. The opposition is pushing for a constitutional amendment to grant broad amnesty to those involved in the riot, while the PT, PV, and PCdoB defend the Court’s decision. Zema accused Moraes of 'overrunning Congress' and considering himself 'untouchable'.

item.title: Neymar, Rayan, Pedro: jogadores que ainda buscam vaga na Copa tentam sprint final para convencer Ancelotti
item.description: With just one week left until Brazil's 2026 World Cup squad announcement, players like Neymar, Rayan, Igor Jesus, João Pedro, and Pedro are pushing for final spots in Carlo Ancelotti's list. Some are showcasing form in decisive Premier League and FA Cup matches, while others face uncertainty due to injuries or recent fitness concerns. The roster will be revealed on the 18th at the Museum of Tomorrow in Rio de Janeiro.

item.title: Lula caminha na Granja do Torto 16 dias após cirurgia
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was seen walking at the Granja do Torto residence 16 days after undergoing surgery to remove a basal cell carcinoma from his scalp. The procedure, performed on April 24 at the Sírio-Libanês Hospital, was deemed minor with no subsequent restrictions. Lula also received a corticosteroid injection in his right thumb to treat tendinitis, both procedures approved by medical officials.

item.title: Bolsonarista publica vídeo bebendo detergente Ypê
item.description: A Bolsonaro supporter published a video drinking Ypê detergent while making obscene gestures toward PT supporters. The video spreads as a meme on social media, tied to unsubstantiated claims that Lula’s government is using Anvisa to persecute the company, whose owners backed Bolsonaro in 2022. Anvisa had ordered a product recall on May 7 due to manufacturing practice failures, a preventive measure to avoid bacterial contamination risk.

item.title: 68 milhões de brasileiros moram em áreas com presença de facções e milícias, aponta pesquisa
item.description: A survey by the Brazilian Forum of Public Safety and Datafolha finds that 68 million Brazilians (41% of the population) perceive the presence of criminal factions and militias in their neighborhoods, with nearly half describing their activity as 'visible' or 'very visible'. The impact extends beyond fear, affecting daily routines, mobility, and consumption, as organized crime shapes neighborhood rules and exerts territorial control, primarily through the PCC, Red Command, and dozens of other groups.

item.title: Golpes digitais preocupam 83% da população, aponta levantamento
item.description: A survey by the Brazilian Forum of Public Safety in partnership with Datafolha shows that 83.2% of Brazilians fear becoming victims of digital scams, making it the top concern, technically tied with fear of armed robbery (82.3%) and being killed during an assault (80.7%). The report also states that digital scams were the most frequent crime experienced in the last 12 months, affecting 15.8% of the population — approximately 26.3 million people — with notable use of fake automatic CNH renewal as bait.

item.title: Medo da violência altera a rotina de 57% dos brasileiros e afeta mais mulheres e população de baixa renda, diz pesquisa
item.description: A survey by the Brazilian Forum on Public Security and Datafolha shows that 57% of Brazilians changed their routines due to fear of violence in the past 12 months, with 96.2% reporting fear of at least one violent situation. Common adaptations include altering usual routes (36.5%), avoiding going out at night (35.6%), and not carrying cellphones due to robbery fears (33.5%). The burden falls disproportionately on women and low-income populations (classes D/E), who experience more intense and widespread fear, particularly regarding sexual aggression and patrimonial vulnerability.

item.title: 41% dos brasileiros afirmam conviver com o crime organizado no bairro onde moram
item.description: 41.2% of Brazilians aged 16 or older report living with the presence of organized crime in their neighborhoods, according to a report by the Brazilian Forum of Public Security. This equals 68.7 million people, with higher perception in state capitals (55.9%) and spread even to interior cities (34.1%). The influence of these groups on local rules of coexistence is acknowledged by 61.4% of those who recognize them, reflecting a 'criminal governance' and a 'duopoly of violence' alongside the State.

item.title: Às vésperas da eleição, 6 a cada 10 brasileiros têm medo de sofrer agressões por opção política
item.description: 60% of Brazilians fear physical aggression due to their political choices, a level of concern similar to four years ago. The study by the Brazilian Forum of Public Security and Datafolha shows women, poorer classes (D and E), and residents in areas with organized crime presence are most affected, with 2.2% reporting having suffered political violence in the last 12 months.

item.title: Pesquisa indica subnotificação generalizada de roubos de celular e golpes na internet
item.description: A Datafolha survey indicates that underreporting of cellphone theft and internet fraud in Brazil may exceed 90%, with approximately 26.3 million people affected by digital scams and 13.9 million by cellphone robbery/theft in the last 12 months—far above official figures of 2.1 million and 918,000, respectively. Fear of these crimes is widespread, with 96% of respondents expressing concern about becoming victims, particularly of online scams, prompting calls for specific policy proposals from candidates in the 2026 elections.

item.title: Erika e Sâmia acionam órgãos contra Tarcísio após ação da PM na USP
item.description: Federal deputies Erika Hilton and Sâmia Bomfim (PSOL-SP) have filed complaints with the São Paulo State Prosecutor's Office, the Military Police Corregedor, and the Public Ministry against Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, the Military Police, and USP's rectorate following a violent police operation that cleared the university's rectorate occupied by students. They condemned the use of force, lack of judicial authorization, and alleged collusion between police and university authorities, asserting the students' constitutional right to protest.
